properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hardhat (root package.json) is Ethereum L1 tooling used by the devnet's postman tests to simulate L1. hash.js is available in that shipped stack; no first-party JS exists. Changeable here only by pruning dev tooling — not application crypto.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: 3DES is broken independently of quantum computing (Sweet32, 64-bit block) — an outstanding defect to not queue behind PQ work. No 3DES call site exists in starknet_devnet itself; the algorithm ships in the locked library. pycryptodome also provides the keccak256 that eth-hash uses for Ethereum hashing.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Classical ECDSA on the secp256k1 blockchain curve — Shor-vulnerable, deadline-class risk. It belongs to Hardhat/ethereumjs which the devnet uses to simulate L1 in test_postman.py; the Starknet application itself signs on the STARK curve, not secp256k1. Deps are changeable here by pruning/upgrading test tooling.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 13 sites are real digest values (block hashes, compiled class hashes, tx hashes) compared with ==/!= rather than a constant-time compare. Security relevance is low: these are public on-chain values used for sentinel checks (hash == 0), change detection (previous_class_hash != class_hash) and test assertions, not secret MAC verifications — so the timing-leak the rule targets is not exploitable here. The pattern is genuinely present in first-party code (starknet_devnet/util.py:142,190,231, for

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency of the crypto-browserify stack bundled by Hardhat; no first-party call site — the algorithm ships in the dev tooling. Single-round MD5 KDF is the retroactive-risk practice this records; replaceable only by upgrading the toolchain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA here is throwaway keygen for local HTTPS dev certs (selfsigned→Docusaurus `serve --https`), not data protection; Shor-vulnerable key material generation, present in the build but unconfigured. pycryptodome's RSA surface likewise has no first-party call site in starknet_devnet.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the devnet's core key-generation path and a genuine CWE-338 posture issue, but the determinism is the product feature: the seed is printed so the account sequence can be replicated, and the code warns "Use these accounts and their keys ONLY for local testing". The real-world exposure is a developer copying a devnet account to mainnet — 32 bits of seed entropy make the whole account set brute-forceable. Changeable here (secrets/os.urandom would need a redesign of the seed-replication UX).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: itsdangerous is Flask's token-signing layer. The devnet's Flask API (starknet_devnet/blueprints/*) never sets a secret_key and serves plain HTTP over gunicorn, so session/cookie signing is dormant; the algorithm ships in the library and would apply if sessions were enabled. Same package as LIB-abaa340f — that object is the dependency facet, this one the algorithm default.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The devnet's test suite declares and executes custom account contracts whose signatures it verifies with Cairo's ECDSA builtin (starkware.cairo.common.signature.verify_ecdsa_signature on the STARK curve) — this is the account-abstraction signature scheme the tool reproduces, so the ECDSA exposure follows the StarkNet protocol it emulates (replaceable only upstream). The lockfile declarations record which packages ship the ECDSA implementations the build pulls in.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped Hardhat tooling stack; no first-party JS calls it (the repo's only JS is the hardhat L1 simulator and the Docusaurus docs site). Ed25519 signatures are Shor-vulnerable but not harvest-sensitive — deadline-class.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Developer tooling script (not shipped runtime): a one-shot curl downloading the rustup installer with --tlsv1.2 as a minimum-version bound. Admits TLS 1.2 sessions (ECDHE classical key exchange, harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure) though a server supporting only 1.2 is what triggers it; with a modern curl/OpenSSL the session may still negotiate 1.3. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory asset: elliptic@6.5.4 (which provides ECDH over secp256k1/secp256r1 etc.) is a transitive dependency of the root hardhat-project (Ethereum tooling). No first-party ECDH call site in this repo — it ships in node_modules as part of the Hardhat toolchain used for the Solidity L1-messaging test contracts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shor-vulnerable key agreement available in the shipped tooling; no call site in first-party code — presence is what this inventory records. Same library as ALG-683d5cd2/ALG-f58a8f00 (tweetnacl).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory asset, not a call site: the npm pbkdf2 package (^3.0.17) is a transitive dependency of the root package.json, which is a hardhat-project (Solidity tooling for the L1-messaging test contracts) — pbkdf2 there backs Ethereum keystore/scrypt key derivation in the Hardhat/web3.js toolchain. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3/Keccak availability across the build: keccak + @ethersproject/keccak256 are transitive deps of the root hardhat-project (Solidity tooling — and the Solidity test contracts in test/contracts/solidity/ genuinely call keccak256). cairo_rs_py_patch.py:287 configures the Cairo VM's keccak builtin (max size 2**20) — the devnet enables the VM's SHA-3-family builtin so contracts can use it. The compiled Cairo artifacts (UDC OpenZeppelin contract, custom-account fixtures) reference keccak in their

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory asset: scrypt-js is a transitive dependency of the root hardhat-project (Ethereum keystore KDF in the Hardhat/web3.js toolchain). The poetry.lock/pyproject.toml attributions come from pycryptodome (optional extra of eth-hash via web3 ~6.0.0), which ships scrypt. No first-party scrypt call site in starknet_devnet source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two independent availability paths for AES: (1) node-forge@1.3.1 in the page/ subproject's lockfile (an npm library that implements AES among many primitives), (2) the Python build's pycryptodome (optional extra of eth-hash at poetry.lock:362/798, pulled via web3 ~6.0.0) which ships full AES. Neither is a first-party call site in this repo — these record that AES is available in the shipped dependency trees.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped Hardhat tooling; no first-party call site. SHA-256 itself is quantum-adequate (Grover-only) — an inventory line, not a defect.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory asset: BLAKE3 is available via the @noble/hashes package declared in the root package-lock.json. BLAKE3 is a modern hash — Grover only halves its security margin; no first-party call site in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory attribution: SHA-3 via @noble/hashes@1.1.2 in the root package-lock.json. Same logical dependency as the keccak/js-sha3 declarations adjudicated under the SHA-3 object ALG-052c24b2 — availability, no distinct first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Symmetric AEAD — Grover-only quantum impact (not Shor-broken); recorded for inventory completeness of the shipped tooling stack. No first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS transport for the Python toolchain: requests 2.28.2 is a declared dev dependency (pyproject.toml dev group ~2.28) whose HTTPS support rides urllib3/OpenSSL defaults — the same default-settings posture as the confirmed PROTO-dca6de59 (scripts/find_reverted.py polls https://external.integration.starknet.io over requests). Key exchange follows the host OpenSSL (version unknown from the tree), hence the ? rating. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl (XSalsa20-Poly1305 AE, Ed25519 signatures, X25519/Ed25519 key agreement) is declared in the root package-lock.json as part of the hardhat-project dependency tree (node_modules entry at line 3699) — Ethereum tooling for the Solidity L1-messaging test contracts. The algorithms it ships are real availability, with no first-party call site in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.1.2 (SHA-2/SHA-3, BLAKE family, etc.) declared in the root package-lock.json (node_modules entry at line 420) via the hardhat-project tree. It is the carrier behind the confirmed BLAKE3 (ALG-979eccf8) and SHA-3 (ALG-c9ef78a4) dependency attributions.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge is the crypto provider behind selfsigned@2.0.1, which Docusaurus uses for optional `docusaurus serve --https` on the docs site; page/docusaurus.config.js does not enable HTTPS, so the RSA/X.509/TLS surface ships but is unconfigured here. Changeable by pruning/upgrading docs tooling.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Governance/trust artifact: certifi's cacert.pem is what the devnet uses to verify remote Starknet nodes in fork mode (requests/urllib3 over HTTPS to alpha-mainnet etc.). Bundle dated May 2023 — root rotation happens upstream; bumping certifi is changeable here. Same logical asset as LIB-0a1caea6 (the package).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev-only PKI: a self-signed cert for the docs site's local HTTPS server; page/docusaurus.config.js does not enable HTTPS so nothing is provisioned in this repo's config — capability present in the build. Not production trust material.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The X.509 assembly machinery of node-forge (same library as LIB-fe0eb9a4), exercised only by selfsigned's dev cert generation. Different facet of the same provider — kept distinct from the RSA facet ALG-589856a1.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same logical asset as ALG-065af532 (certifi == its CA trust bundle; one package, one payload). Recorded here as the dependency entry so a reader can trace either name to the same trust store.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Carries the devnet's fork-mode HTTPS traffic (remote Starknet networks) with 1.26.x defaults — TLS 1.2-capable classical key exchange, quantum-harvestable transport. Observable here; upgradable by bumping requests/urllib3 (1.26 line is EOL-era). This is the transport layer under LIB-b9851744 (requests).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pycryptodome@3.17 rides into the build as the optional extra of eth-hash (poetry.lock:362,798,798+), pulled via web3 ~6.0.0 — it ships AES, PBKDF2, scrypt, keccak and is the carrier behind the confirmed AES (ALG-0eb2c0da), PBKDF2 (ALG-4de3b020) and scrypt (ALG-c1f8b585) poetry.lock attributions. No first-party pycryptodome import found in starknet_devnet source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pure-Python ecdsa@0.18.0 declared in poetry.lock (line 715) — provides ECDSA over secp256k1/NIST curves on the Python side of the build (pulled via the web3/starkware dependency chain). This is the concrete package behind the confirmed ECDSA object's poetry.lock site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 in the root package-lock.json (hardhat-project tree) — the Ethereum keystore KDF in the Hardhat/web3.js toolchain. Same logical asset as the confirmed scrypt algorithm object.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 (node_modules/elliptic at package-lock.json:1823) — ECDH/ECDSA over secp256k1/secp256r1 etc. in the hardhat-project tree. Same logical asset as the confirmed ECDH object (ALG-c9ffc8a8), which resolves ECDH through this package.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

Same logical dependency as the poetry.lock entry (LIB-961b6c54). No first-party werkzeug.security call site found.
